title: Chapter 2908 - 161: Divine Slave_2
content:
Chapter 2908: Chapter 161: Divine Slave_2

Moreover, Mo Hua is not yet skilled at skeletal engraving within the human body. It’s already challenging to engrave the Twelve Meridian Spirit Bone Formation, and it’s uncertain whether it will succeed.

Adding the Wood Revitalization Formation is too difficult. This is something that can only be considered later.

One must eat a meal bite by bite. Currently, it’s crucial to first become familiar with "Golden Jade Bone Casting," "Spirit Remains Bone Engraving," and the specific application of the Twelve Scripture Gluttonous Spirit Corpse Formation.

Mo Hua began to focus and proceed with engraving the Spiritual Corpse Formation on Sishen’s bones according to his own ideas.

This entire set of operations and formations is too complex, and extremely eerie and profound.

Mo Hua worked for a full two days and ultimately still failed.

There were many reasons for the failure, such as Sishen’s bones being too hard, the corpse temperature being too low, the poor fusion between golden jade and the corpse, the poor usability of the tools for bone engraving, the difficulty of drawing Taotie Patterns, the incompleteness of the Formation Pivot with the human body’s meridians, and so on.

Mo Hua sighed but was not too disappointed.

This kind of thing cannot be accomplished in one go, or done once and succeeded.

Every success must go through countless failures.

By identifying the root causes of failure, thinking about them one by one, solving them one by one, and eventually eliminating all ’failures,’ success will naturally follow.

Thus, ’success’ and ’failure’ are two sides of the same coin, one and the same.

Mo Hua adjusted his mindset, patiently summarized the experiences, and then started to try again.

In this process of trying, constantly discovering problems, constantly solving problems, constantly overcoming failures...

Mo Hua’s understanding of bone casting, bone engraving, and the Ultimate Taotie Spirit Remains Formation also constantly deepened, and the operation became increasingly proficient.

At the same time, in another direction, his research on corpses, experience in "corpse control," and ability to transform human body meridians and skeletons via formations also deepened unexpectedly...

Although this experience and ability are somewhat... unlike what a serious cultivator should have.

Mo Hua, in his heart, was also very resistant.

But there was no choice; having embarked on this Core Formation path, exploring bone casting, bone engraving, and Spirit Formation Patterns, the experience naturally came.

Mo Hua wanted to reject it, but he could not...

...

While Mo Hua was applying and transforming the formations on Sishen’s corpse bones.

The unification and rectification of various tribes within the Vermilion Bird Mountain Realm continued to advance.

These plans, under the name of the Divine Lord, were directed by Mo Hua and fully handled by Dan Zhu, with Lugu, Dan Lie, and other Great Chiefs assisting from the side, implemented almost universally in all tribes throughout the Vermilion Bird Mountain Realm...

Dan Zhu was responsible for this matter.

Dan Zhu had a heart of sincerity, honesty, and kindness, with a steadfast Taoist Heart, and followed Mo Hua for the longest time; he was also the person Mo Hua most trusted and recognized in the Great Wilderness.

Whether now or in the future, Mo Hua hopes Dan Zhu can grow into an outstanding tribe leader.

Whether he is present or not, he can independently govern the tribes in the Barbaric Wilderness, providing a foundation for the livelihood and stability of the wild populace.

However, Dan Zhu is currently only in the Initial Golden Core stage, somewhat lacking in realm and with unstable foundations.

Thus, Mo Hua had Dan Lie and Lugu step in, leveraging the prestige of the Alliance Hierarch and the Great Chiefs, to assist Dan Zhu in this endeavor.

Nominally, everyone is working for the "Divine Lord," in the name of the "Shaman."

But Mo Hua’s expectations for Dan Zhu run the deepest.

Because Mo Hua can see, among the Barbarian Cultivators of the various tribes in the Great Wilderness, only Dan Zhu’s heart is like the burning flame of the Vermilion Bird, the most "vivid red" and passionate.

And the main purpose of Mo Hua’s initiatives is "to align allies and suppress enemies."

Those who embrace change flourish, those who resist perish.

Taking advantage of the Divine Lord’s manifestation during the previous Vermilion Bird Mountain battle, slaying the Witch Vulture God’s "divine power" is not yet dissipated.

Taking advantage of the peak faith in the Divine Lord in the hearts of all tribal barbarian cultivators.

Mo Hua must seize the opportunity to enforce reforms under the name of the Divine Lord and with the commands of the Shaman within the main tribes, to thoroughly consolidate power.

To those who sincerely submit, Mo Hua grants them higher status and positions.

Those with ulterior motives are suppressed and marginalized, gradually pushed away from the power center.

And those harboring rebellious intent, or even attempting a coup, are directly executed.

Power struggles have always been cold and ruthless, with no room for naive warmth, or else death is the only outcome.

Additionally, Mo Hua began to unify the tribes’ faiths.

Forcibly eradicating the original beliefs of other tribes was too radical, likely to provoke resistance and backlash. Thus, Mo Hua allowed each tribe to retain its own beliefs, while uniformly requiring them all to worship the "Divine Lord."

And to place faith in the Divine Lord above each tribe’s indigenous beliefs.

In this way, the "Divine Lord" truly becomes the "Lord of all gods" in the Great Wilderness.

No tribe’s beliefs are to conflict with those regarding the Divine Lord, otherwise, it will be seen as heresy, to be suppressed.

Their tribal deities will also be opportunistically confronted and "devoured" by Mo Hua.

And the "faith" in the Divine Lord is not merely blind superstition or belief.

Mo Hua personally crafted doctrines and, through these doctrines, transformed this "belief" into "ideals."

These doctrines include but are not limited to the Divine Lord protecting the Great Wilderness, shielding its people, and forbidding any tribe from harming the Great Wilderness’s unity and stability.

Among the barbarian cultivators, equality is determined by belief. At the very least, basic rights such as life are equal.

Power and status may differ, but faith in the Divine Lord is singular, supreme.
